claim: Dewey's five phases (difficulty, definition, suggestion, reasoning, test) are a non-fixed cycle with fusion and back-steps, not a strict sequence; Dewey himself and Hitchcock (SEP) say so.
agent_test: Allow free back-edges in the state graph; compare forward-only order vs graph with back-edges at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Dewey 1910 itself states fusion of steps one and two and 'no cast-iron rules'; 'phases not steps', no invariant sequence, spiral and redefinition come from SEP (Hitchcock), not Dewey 1910.

claim: There is no controlled empirical test that the Dewey stage order (or any critical-thinking stage order) causes better thinking; the model is conceptual and descriptive. Narrowing (gap search): step order inside a rationale and premise order do matter causally (d01, d02), but these are not stage-order tests.
agent_test: Run an order ablation on our agent: permute and skip S-stages at equal tokens on the same items.
audit_note: Negative claim; SEP entry reports no stage-order test, and the Wang et al. and Chen et al. numbers match.

claim: Defining the problem before proposing solutions is claimed by Dewey to separate controlled from random inference; in LLMs, plan-then-solve gives small gains (+3.1 average points over zero-shot CoT, text-davinci-003, six math sets) and barely cuts missing-step errors (12% to 10% of failures).
agent_test: Ablate the define stage (skip vs run) at equal tokens on math and underspecified items.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction (no external signal) does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8, GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds.
agent_test: Compare a review/revise loop with and without an external check at equal tokens; count right-to-wrong flips.
audit_note: Evidence line c04 misattributes oracle-table numbers but the claim's own numbers (CSQA 75.8 to 41.8, GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0) match Huang Table 3.

claim: Self-correction helps when a reliable external signal exists (oracle labels: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, CSQA 75.8 to 89.7, HotpotQA 26.0 to 29.0; GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59; CRITIC with tools +7.7 F1 on QA, +7.0 on math).
agent_test: Gate the revise step on a tool or executable check; ablate the gate.
audit_note: Minor: CRITIC +7.7 F1 and +7.0 are for ChatGPT; oracle-label numbers match Huang Table 2 (oracle labels are an unrealistic signal per Huang).

claim: Self-critique alone, without tools, adds little: CRITIC ablation -0.03 and +2.33 F1; Self-Refine math 64.1 to 64.1; self-verification +2.33% average.
agent_test: Measure the marginal value of a pure self-critique pass vs the same tokens spent on a second independent sample.
audit_note: Minor: the +2.33% self-verification figure is Weng et al.'s backward-verification average gain on Instruct-GPT, a real small gain rather than plain self-critique; it coincides numerically with CRITIC's +2.33 F1.

claim: Self-Refine style loops help on preference-judged tasks (sentiment 8.8 to 30.4 GPT-3.5, dialogue 36.4 to 63.6) but not on math; task type is the boundary condition. Caveat: gains are scored by model-based metrics.
agent_test: Apply a critique loop only to open-ended items; check it on math items.

claim: Reflexion-style verbal reflection with an environment signal gives gains (ALFWorld +22, HotPotQA +20, HumanEval +11 points), consistent with the external-signal rule.
agent_test: Retry with stored reflection only after an external failure signal; compare with blind resampling.

claim: Self-selected reasoning structures help: Self-Discover PaLM 2-L BBH 56 to 67, T4D 30 to 69; GPT-4 BBH 58 to 81, T4D 51 to 85, MATH 70.5 to 73. The gain over CoT on MATH is small (+1.5 to +3).
agent_test: Let the agent compose its own stage plan per item vs a fixed plan at equal tokens.

claim: Letting the model choose the order of cognitive operations (Cognitive Prompting) gives about 95% on GSM8K with Llama 70B (hybrid with few-shot CoT); the commonest self-chosen order was goal clarification, decomposition, pattern recognition. Gains were larger for mid-size models.
agent_test: Compare fixed vs self-chosen operator order at equal tokens; log chosen orders.
audit_note: Both listed evidence lines are the same paper (Kramer and Baumann, 2410.02953), so only one distinct source; its text supports every stated point (95% is the hybrid H-CP on LLaMA 70B, GC-DC-PR most frequent SA-CP sequence, proportional gain larger for mid-size).

claim: Critical-question checklists inside the prompt (CQoT, Toulmin-based) give modest judged gains: +4.61% reasoning, +5.4% math on MT-Bench, best in 18 of 20 comparisons, but one model lost to CoT on some tasks.
agent_test: Add critical-question review with a loop cap; compare with the same tokens spent on extra CoT samples.

claim: Extra reasoning can inflate length without value: reasoning models spend over 3,000 tokens on missing-premise questions vs about 1,000 on well-posed ones, and do not stop.
agent_test: Add a premise-check and stop rule; measure tokens and accuracy on missing-premise items.

claim: Correction gains depend on base accuracy: in math, critique-correction gains show only when generation accuracy exceeds about 41%; logic-oriented tasks are more correctable.
agent_test: Gate review on a first-pass confidence signal; test on items below and above that accuracy.

claim: Instruction in critical thinking has a small positive effect overall (g+ = 0.30, 341 effects); mixed teaching (explicit principles plus content application) is highest by approach at 0.38, and the dialogue+anchored+mentoring combination reaches 0.57.
agent_test: Not directly testable; analogue is explicit stage instructions plus worked examples vs either alone.
audit_note: Minor: the mixed-approach advantage (0.38 vs 0.23-0.29) is not statistically significant per SEP, which the claim omits; TUM summary calls 341 'studies' while SEP says 341 effect sizes.

claim: College gains in critical thinking are about 0.6 SD over four years (50th to 72nd percentile), nonlinear, with no clear major differences.
agent_test: None; context only.

claim: Expert consensus (Delphi, 46 experts, six rounds) names six core skills (interpretation, analysis, evaluation, inference, explanation, self-regulation). This is a skills list, not a stage order, and the panel was about 52% philosophers.
agent_test: Map S1-S9 to the six skills to find gaps (interpretation, self-regulation).

claim: Coders applying the four-phase practical-inquiry model (trigger, exploration, integration, resolution) reached kappa 0.74 only on the third transcript after three training sessions (earlier kappas .35 and .49); in that study exploration was the most frequent phase (42%), integration 13% and resolution 4%, and most coding disagreement was between exploration and integration; a later study cited by the CoI authors reported 20% of contributions at the highest phases.
agent_test: Log where the agent stalls (exploration without integration); add a forced integrate step and compare.
audit_note: Kappa 0.74 was reached only on the third transcript after three training sessions (earlier kappas .35 and .49); 42% exploration is the largest share, not 'most'; the '1 to 18% across reviews' resolution range is not in the opened sources (Akyol et al. cite 20% at the highest phases).
claim_before_audit: Human coders can apply a four-phase inquiry model (trigger, exploration, integration, resolution) reliably (kappa 0.74), but most messages stay in exploration (42%) and few reach resolution (4% in one study; 1 to 18% across reviews). Exploration and integration are the most confused labels.

claim: Humans judging LLM answers follow the LLM: when the LLM is wrong, participants were correct only 24.5% (short), 54.2% (medium), 30.7% (long) of the time (N=24, 15 Watson-Glaser items); when right, 71.5/81.1/79.5%.
agent_test: Test whether our answer length and justification change a judge model's error detection.

claim: LLM scoring of critical-thinking essays is mediocre: GPT-5 zero-shot accuracy .543 vs fine-tuned Llama 8B .604 on 500 coded essays; human kappa up to 0.87 on evidence evaluation.
agent_test: Warning that LLM judges of reasoning quality are noisy; calibrate any judge against humans.

claim: Stage-structured Polya-style instruction tuning makes a model follow stages (stage-protocol errors 0.0% for polya-v2 vs higher for base), but this measures adherence, not answer-correctness gain.
agent_test: Measure adherence to the state graph separately from answer accuracy.

claim: Dewey is named in only one of the opened LLM prompting papers (Atomic Reasoner, which maps its actions onto Dewey's five steps) and Hitchcock in none; the other stage-prompting papers (Self-Discover, Plan-and-Solve, Cognitive Prompting) reach a Dewey-like cycle by convergence (Polya, Toulmin), so LLM evidence supports staged prompting loosely, not Dewey specifically.
agent_test: None; guards against over-claiming lineage.
audit_note: Atomic Reasoner (2503.15944) names Dewey, cites How We Think and has an appendix mapping its actions onto Dewey's five steps, so Dewey is named in an opened LLM paper (Hitchcock is not).
claim_before_audit: Dewey and Hitchcock are not named in the opened LLM prompting papers; the Dewey-like cycle is reached by convergence (Polya, Toulmin), so LLM evidence supports staged prompting loosely, not Dewey specifically.

claim: Order of steps inside a reasoning chain is causal in LLMs: breaking step order cut GSM8K answer accuracy from 48.5 to 23.1 (text-davinci-002); permuting premises cut deduction accuracy by over 30 points. Validity of each step mattered much less (39.5).
agent_test: Permute S3-S8 order on the same items at equal tokens; expect large drops if order carries information.

claim: With a sound external verifier, plain re-sampling nearly equals critique loops at lower token cost (Game of 24: critique 36-38%, resampling k=25 42%, GPT-4); LLM self-critique alone collapses (3%).
agent_test: Compare review loop vs k independent samples + verifier at equal tokens.

claim: Revision gating needs an error-location signal; even a roughly 65%-accurate classifier makes backtracking net-positive, but revising already-correct traces costs accuracy.
agent_test: Add a no-error output and a location output to the review stage; measure loss on already-correct items.

claim: Reasoning models do not show the self-correction blind spot; appending Wait lifts non-reasoning models close to their reasoning counterparts (Qwen3-14B 0.117 to 0.868 vs 0.843 in reasoning mode). Explicit review scaffolds are likely redundant on reasoning models.
schema_part: S9 on reasoning vs base models
agent_test: Test scaffold on/off per model class; use a one-word re-entry cue on base models.

claim: Stop rules that work for the test stage: confidence-gated early exit (DEER: length -19% to -80%, accuracy +0.3 to +5.0), answer repetition (convergence at about 60% of steps), trained probes. The first solution is correct in over 92% of cases on easy sets.
agent_test: Implement stop-after-k-identical-trial-answers; compare to a fixed budget.
audit_note: Minor: Liu and Wang report unsupervised stop rules become unstable on MATH-500 and GPQA, so 'work' is conditional; the 92% figure is read from a figure of QwQ/R1 on easy sets.

claim: Solving a fully specified problem does not imply asking the right clarifying question: models reach 40-50% on Logic-Q and Planning-Q (QuestBench) despite over 80% on the math sets; chain of thought gave no significant gain.
agent_test: Add a what-is-missing step with checked output; test on QuestBench-style items.

claim: LLM judges match humans on answer preference (GPT-4 85% vs human-human 81%) but error-step location needs reasoning-class models (ProcessBench F1 o1-mini 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9); stage-adherence judging has no published validation.
agent_test: Validate any stage-adherence judge on 100 human-labelled traces before use.

claim: Review versus resampling depends on difficulty: sequential revision wins on easy-to-medium items, parallel sampling or search on hard ones (Snell 2024, about 4x less compute than best-of-N).
agent_test: Route by an easy/hard estimate; compare to a fixed policy.
